# dx8wasm

> A clean-room DirectX-8 → WebAssembly (WebGL2) translation SDK for porting
> DX8-era Windows games to the browser. It provides the D3D8 API, a fixed-function
> pipeline, a window/input runtime contract, and a tiered Win32→POSIX compat
> layer, so a game compiled with Emscripten runs unmodified against the browser's
> WebGL2 and the emscripten filesystem.

dx8wasm is a reusable SDK, not a single game port. The graphics pipeline is
broadly feature-complete (transforms, all light types, ambient/diffuse/specular,
fog, texture combiners, render states, pre-transformed 2D, every primitive type),
verified by 35 headless pixel/self-test smokes on Linux CI. Two audiences: agents
*building a game against* the SDK (start with SDK_REFERENCE + INTEGRATION), and
agents *contributing to* the SDK (start with AGENTS + ARCHITECTURE). Core
disciplines: clean-room re-derivation, and "flag + fall back + count" for anything
unimplemented (never silently wrong).

## Build against the SDK (consumers)

- [SDK reference](docs/SDK_REFERENCE.md): the complete callable surface — D3D8 API subset, the runtime contract (init/input/coverage), the compatlib tiers, and the load-bearing conventions (color order, matrix convention, coordinate mapping).
- [Integration guide](docs/INTEGRATION.md): the five steps to wire a real game (build/link, D3D8 include, init, non-blocking main loop, assets) with a coverage-driven gap-filling workflow.
- [Integration example](examples/minigame/minigame.cpp): a keyboard-controlled sprite using only the public surface — the concrete template.
- [Conformance matrix](docs/CONFORMANCE.md): exactly which D3D8 states/ops/formats are handled vs fall back (probed empirically).
- [Compatlib map](docs/COMPATLIB.md): the tiered Win32 surface a game needs, with POSIX mappings and build order.

## Contribute to the SDK (maintainers)

- [Agent instructions](AGENTS.md): build/test/run commands, repo layout, the non-negotiable conventions, and the "how to add a feature" pattern.
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the layer map, the libraries, the draw-call data flow, the test harness, and the known gotchas.
- [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md): phases, what's done, what's next.
- [Porting methodology](docs/PORTING_METHOD.md): the general method that applies to any classic-game port.

## Optional

- [README](README.md): project summary, status, quickstart.
- [Spec](SPEC.md): the original design.
- [Licensing](docs/LICENSING.md): GPL-3.0-only, clean-room stance, reference-source status.
